title: Java Platform Architecture and Core Fundamentals
content:
Java is a class-based, object-oriented programming language designed for portability ('Write Once, Run Anywhere').

Platform Architecture:
- JDK (Java Development Kit): Includes compiler (javac), debugger, and documentation.
- JRE (Java Runtime Environment): Provides libraries and runtime environment.
- JVM (Java Virtual Machine): Executes compiled bytecode (.class files) via Just-In-Time (JIT) compilation to native machine code.

Primitive Types vs Reference Types:
- Primitives: byte, short, int, long, float, double, boolean, char (stored directly on stack).
- Reference Types: Objects, Arrays, Strings (stored on heap, referenced by stack variables).

Basic Structure:
public class Main {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello, Adaptive Java Learner!");
    }
}

Common Mistakes:
1. Comparing Strings using == instead of .equals(): == checks memory reference equality, whereas .equals() compares character contents.
2. NullPointerException: Accessing methods or fields on an object variable that currently points to null.
3. Case sensitivity with class file names: In Java, public class Main must be saved in Main.java.
analogy: The JDK is a factory with tools. The Bytecode is a universal blueprint. The JVM is a local construction robot in each country that reads the blueprint and builds the house using local materials.
simplification_tips: Always remember that Java is strictly typed. Every variable must have a declared type before you can store a value in it.
